The Azéma–Yor transform provides a model-independent mechanism to map any unconstrained wealth process X̂ into a constrained one ^αX̂ that retains the numéraire property. This allows for a principled way to enforce a maximum drawdown level α without relying on specific model assumptions. The transformation ensures that the resulting portfolio is asymptotically optimal among all constrained strategies. The key mathematical duality lies in the fact that the constrained numéraire is derived from the unconstrained one through a pathwise operation that preserves martingale structure. In practice, this requires discretization of continuous-time dynamics to weekly intervals for implementation in GSE, where the α parameter governs the fraction of capital allocated to the risky asset. Failure occurs when the discrete approximation violates the drawdown bound or when α is too restrictive, leading to suboptimal performance.
